annotations.text:
The logging flow reads left to right.

Home carries the last three weeks at day resolution, today's blocks, and the one free-text line. LOG A BLOCK opens the lane picker; picking a lane opens the grid. Two taps after the lane, and the lane's why-sentence is on screen while you answer.

Every phone artboard is 393 x 873 — the Galaxy A52's viewport.

The payoff view. 52 columns, one per week, five lanes.

The thing to judge: BODY going quiet from March to November. Nothing in the app mentions it — the shape just says so. If that doesn't land at a glance, the encoding is wrong, not the concept.

The two questions the README leaves open, drawn rather than argued.

Row 1 is the day mark; row 2 is the week cell, shown at true size and at 3x. The highlighted border marks what the four screens above currently use — A and 1. Each caption names the cost, including for the ones I'd reject.
